entries.statement: For Re(s) > 1, ζ(s) = Σ n^{-s} = Π_p (1 - p^{-s})^{-1}, both converging absolutely.
aliases: zeta has an euler product for re s greater than 1

entries.statement: ζ(s) ≠ 0 for Re(s) > 1.
aliases: zeta has no zeros with real part greater than 1
ζ(s) has no zeros in Re(s) > 1

entries.statement: ζ(s) extends meromorphically to ℂ with a single simple pole at s = 1 of residue 1.
aliases: zeta has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1
ζ has a simple pole at 1 with residue 1
entries.citation: B. Riemann, Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse, Monatsberichte der Berliner Akademie, 1859.

entries.statement: The completed function ξ(s) = ½ s(s-1) π^{-s/2} Γ(s/2) ζ(s) is entire and satisfies ξ(s) = ξ(1-s).
aliases: functional equation of the riemann zeta function
entries.citation: B. Riemann, Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse, Monatsberichte der Berliner Akademie, 1859.

entries.statement: The zeros of ζ(s) with Re(s) < 0 are exactly the simple zeros at s = -2, -4, -6, ….
aliases: trivial zeros of zeta at the negative even integers
ζ(-2n) = 0 for every positive integer n

entries.statement: The nontrivial zeros of ζ are symmetric about the real axis and about the line Re(s) = 1/2: if ρ is a zero, so are ρ̄, 1-ρ and 1-ρ̄.
aliases: nontrivial zeros are symmetric about the critical line
if ρ is a nontrivial zero then so is 1-ρ
entries.attribution: functional equation and ζ(s̄) = conj ζ(s)

entries.statement: ξ(s) is an entire function of order 1 and has a Hadamard product over the nontrivial zeros ρ of ζ.
aliases: ξ is entire of order one
entries.citation: J. Hadamard, Étude sur les propriétés des fonctions entières et en particulier d'une fonction considérée par Riemann, J. Math. Pures Appl. (4) 9 (1893).

entries.statement: ζ(1 + it) ≠ 0 for every real t.
aliases: zeta has no zeros on the line re s = 1
ζ(s) has no zeros on Re(s) = 1
entries.citation: J. Hadamard, Sur la distribution des zéros de la fonction ζ(s) et ses conséquences arithmétiques, Bull. Soc. Math. France 24 (1896).

entries.statement: Prime number theorem: π(x) ~ x / log x, equivalently ψ(x) ~ x.
entries.citation: C.-J. de la Vallée Poussin, Recherches analytiques sur la théorie des nombres premiers, Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles 20 (1896).

entries.statement: The prime number theorem has a proof that does not use complex analysis.
aliases: elementary proof of the prime number theorem
entries.citation: A. Selberg, An elementary proof of the prime-number theorem, Ann. of Math. 50 (1949).

entries.statement: There is c > 0 such that ζ(σ + it) ≠ 0 for σ ≥ 1 - c / log(|t| + 2).
aliases: de la vallée poussin zero-free region

entries.statement: There is c > 0 such that ζ(σ + it) ≠ 0 for σ ≥ 1 - c / ((log |t|)^{2/3} (log log |t|)^{1/3}) and |t| ≥ 3.
Riemann–von Mangoldt formula: N(T) = (T/2π) log(T/2π) - T/2π + O(log T).
entries.attribution: stated by Riemann (1859); proved by von Mangoldt (1905)

entries.statement: For x > 1, ψ₀(x) = x - Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ - log(2π) - ½ log(1 - x^{-2}), the sum over nontrivial zeros taken symmetrically.
entries.citation: H. von Mangoldt, Zu Riemanns Abhandlung "Über die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse", J. reine angew. Math. 114 (1895).

entries.statement: ζ has infinitely many zeros on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.
aliases: infinitely many zeros on the critical line
the riemann zeta function has infinitely many zeros on the critical line
zeta has infinitely many zeros on the critical line
entries.citation: G. H. Hardy, Sur les zéros de la fonction ζ(s) de Riemann, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 158 (1914).

entries.statement: N₀(T) ≫ T, where N₀(T) counts zeros 1/2 + iγ with 0 < γ ≤ T.
aliases: hardy-littlewood lower bound for zeros on the critical line
entries.citation: G. H. Hardy and J. E. Littlewood, The zeros of Riemann's zeta-function on the critical line, Math. Z. 10 (1921).

entries.statement: A positive proportion of the nontrivial zeros of ζ lie on the critical line.
aliases: positive proportion of zeros on the critical line
a positive proportion of zeros lie on the critical line
entries.citation: A. Selberg, On the zeros of Riemann's zeta-function, Skr. Norske Vid. Akad. Oslo I (1942).

entries.statement: More than one third of the nontrivial zeros of ζ lie on the critical line.
entries.citation: N. Levinson, More than one third of zeros of Riemann's zeta-function are on σ = 1/2, Adv. Math. 13 (1974).

entries.statement: More than two fifths of the nontrivial zeros of ζ lie on the critical line.
entries.citation: J. B. Conrey, More than two fifths of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line, J. reine angew. Math. 399 (1989).

entries.statement: For every ε > 0, all but o(N(T)) of the nontrivial zeros with 0 < γ ≤ T satisfy |β - 1/2| < ε.
aliases: almost all zeros are arbitrarily close to the critical line

entries.statement: N(σ, T) ≪ T^{3(1-σ)/(2-σ)} (log T)^5 uniformly for 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1.
entries.citation: A. E. Ingham, On the estimation of N(σ, T), Quart. J. Math. 11 (1940).

entries.statement: Riemann–Siegel formula: Z(t) = 2 Σ_{n ≤ √(t/2π)} n^{-1/2} cos(θ(t) - t log n) + O(t^{-1/4}).
entries.citation: C. L. Siegel, Über Riemanns Nachlaß zur analytischen Zahlentheorie, Quellen und Studien zur Geschichte der Mathematik, Astronomie und Physik, Abt. B 2 (1932).

entries.statement: Turing's method: an upper bound on ∫ S(t) dt lets one certify that all zeros up to a height T have been found by sign changes of Z(t).
entries.citation: A. M. Turing, Some calculations of the Riemann zeta-function, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 3 (1953).

entries.statement: All nontrivial zeros of ζ with 0 < Im(ρ) ≤ 3·10^12 lie on the critical line and are simple.
aliases: riemann hypothesis verified up to height 3 10 12
entries.citation: D. Platt and T. Trudgian, The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3·10^12, Bull. London Math. Soc. 53 (2021).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to π(x) = li(x) + O(√x log x).
aliases: rh iff pi(x) = li(x) + o(sqrt x log x)
entries.citation: H. von Koch, Sur la distribution des nombres premiers, Acta Math. 24 (1901).

entries.statement: Assuming RH, |π(x) - li(x)| < √x log x / (8π) for x ≥ 2657.
entries.citation: L. Schoenfeld, Sharper bounds for the Chebyshev functions θ(x) and ψ(x). II, Math. Comp. 30 (1976).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to M(x) = O(x^{1/2+ε}) for every ε > 0, where M is the Mertens function.
The Mertens conjecture |M(x)| < √x for all x > 1 is false.
entries.citation: A. M. Odlyzko and H. J. J. te Riele, Disproof of the Mertens conjecture, J. reine angew. Math. 357 (1985).

entries.statement: π(x) - li(x) changes sign infinitely often.
entries.citation: J. E. Littlewood, Sur la distribution des nombres premiers, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 158 (1914).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to σ(n) < e^γ n log log n for all n > 5040.
aliases: robin's inequality is equivalent to rh
rh is equivalent to robin's inequality
entries.citation: G. Robin, Grandes valeurs de la fonction somme des diviseurs et hypothèse de Riemann, J. Math. Pures Appl. 63 (1984).

entries.statement: σ(n) < e^γ n log log n + 0.6483 n / log log n for all n ≥ 3.
entries.citation: G. Robin, Grandes valeurs de la fonction somme des diviseurs et hypothèse de Riemann, J. Math. Pures Appl. 63 (1984).

entries.statement: limsup_{n→∞} σ(n) / (n log log n) = e^γ.
entries.citation: T. H. Gronwall, Some asymptotic expressions in the theory of numbers, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 14 (1913).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to σ(n) ≤ H_n + exp(H_n) log H_n for all n ≥ 1, with equality only for n = 1.
entries.citation: J. C. Lagarias, An elementary problem equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis, Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to λ_n ≥ 0 for all n ≥ 1, where λ_n = Σ_ρ [1 - (1 - 1/ρ)^n].
aliases: li coefficients are nonnegative iff rh
entries.citation: X.-J. Li, The positivity of a sequence of numbers and the Riemann hypothesis, J. Number Theory 65 (1997).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to the density in L²(0,1) of the span of the functions x ↦ {θ/x} - θ{1/x}, 0 < θ ≤ 1.
entries.citation: A. Beurling, A closure problem related to the Riemann zeta-function, Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 41 (1955).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to Σ_{k≥1} (-x)^k / ((k-1)! ζ(2k)) = O(x^{1/4+ε}) as x → ∞.
entries.citation: M. Riesz, Sur l'hypothèse de Riemann, Acta Math. 40 (1916).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to ζ'(s) having no zeros in 0 < Re(s) < 1/2.
entries.citation: A. Speiser, Geometrisches zur Riemannschen Zetafunktion, Math. Ann. 110 (1934).

entries.statement: RH is equivalent to the positivity of Weil's explicit-formula functional on test functions of the form f * f̃.
RH is equivalent to the hyperbolicity of all Jensen polynomials of the Taylor coefficients of ξ at s = 1/2.
entries.attribution: Pólya (1927); partial results Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier (2019)
entries.citation: M. Griffin, K. Ono, L. Rolen and D. Zagier, Jensen polynomials for the Riemann zeta function and other sequences, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 116 (2019).

entries.statement: The de Bruijn–Newman constant satisfies Λ ≤ 1/2.
entries.citation: N. G. de Bruijn, The roots of trigonometric integrals, Duke Math. J. 17 (1950).

entries.statement: The de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ is finite (Λ > -∞), and RH is equivalent to Λ ≤ 0.
aliases: newman's theorem on the de bruijn-newman constant
entries.citation: C. M. Newman, Fourier transforms with only real zeros, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 61 (1976).

entries.statement: The de Bruijn–Newman constant satisfies Λ ≥ 0.
aliases: the de bruijn-newman constant is non-negative
the de bruijn–newman constant is non-negative
entries.citation: B. Rodgers and T. Tao, The de Bruijn–Newman constant is non-negative, Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020).

entries.statement: There exist Dirichlet series satisfying a Riemann-type functional equation that have zeros off the critical line, so a functional equation alone does not imply an analogue of RH.
aliases: functional equation alone does not imply rh

entries.statement: Voronin universality: any non-vanishing continuous function on a closed disc of radius < 1/4 centred at 3/4, holomorphic inside, is uniformly approximated by vertical shifts ζ(s + iτ).
ζ(1/2 + it) ≪ |t|^{1/4+ε} (convexity bound, via Phragmén–Lindelöf).
aliases: convexity bound for zeta on the critical line

entries.citation: J. Bourgain, Decoupling, exponential sums and the Riemann zeta function, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 30 (2017).

entries.statement: RH implies the Lindelöf hypothesis ζ(1/2 + it) ≪ |t|^ε.
Assuming RH, the pair correlation of normalized zeros matches 1 - (sin πu / πu)² for test functions with Fourier support in (-1, 1).
entries.citation: H. L. Montgomery, The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 24 (1973).

entries.statement: ζ(0) = -1/2 and ζ(1-n) = -B_n/n for n ≥ 2, where B_n are Bernoulli numbers.
ζ(σ) < 0 for real σ in (0, 1); in particular ζ has no real zeros in the critical strip.
aliases: zeta has no real zeros in the critical strip
entries.attribution: standard, via the Dirichlet eta function

entries.statement: ζ(3) is irrational.
entries.citation: R. Apéry, Irrationalité de ζ(2) et ζ(3), Astérisque 61 (1979).

entries.statement: Infinitely many of the values ζ(2n+1), n ≥ 1, are irrational.
entries.citation: K. Ball and T. Rivoal, Irrationalité d'une infinité de valeurs de la fonction zêta aux entiers impairs, Invent. Math. 146 (2001).

entries.statement: The Riemann hypothesis holds for the zeta function of a smooth projective curve over a finite field.
aliases: riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields

entries.statement: The Riemann hypothesis part of the Weil conjectures holds for smooth projective varieties over finite fields.
aliases: deligne's proof of the weil conjectures
entries.citation: P. Deligne, La conjecture de Weil. I, Publ. Math. IHÉS 43 (1974).
